findings.description: Critical: openspec/schemas/consensus-report.schema.json:74 leaves revision-2 policy, match, adjudication, source evidence, and applied-adjudication shapes unconstrained, while consensus_synthesizer.py validates this weaker production schema and convergence_loop.py duplicates only partial relational checks. A critical unreviewed fix can use integer-zero policy flags and zero blocker counts; both validators accept it and convergence treats it as non-blocking.
findings.resolution: Make the production and installed consensus schemas implement the frozen consensus-policy contract, move schema plus relational validation into one shared function, and require both every producer and convergence consumer to call it. Add regressions for non-boolean policy values, missing revision-2 fields, and false-zero summaries.

findings.description: Critical: openspec/schemas/consensus-report.schema.json:26 rejects the supported reviewer identity claude_code and the established gen-eval behavioral source/type. The newly mandatory write validation therefore fails for supported dispatcher and behavioral-review inputs.
findings.resolution: Align the production and installed schema vocabulary with configured vendor identities and review-findings types, including claude_code, gen-eval, and behavioral_failure, and add end-to-end write validation fixtures for those sources.

findings.description: Critical: skills/autopilot/scripts/convergence_loop.py:286 converts every raw ReviewResult.success and finding into synthesis input after using the shared predicate only for the quorum precheck. Two eligible chains plus one success-only result without attempt provenance serialize quorum_received=3 and allow the ineligible finding to change consensus even though the shared eligible count is 2.
findings.resolution: Derive one distinct eligible-terminal-vendor result set through the shared predicate, use it for checkpoints, quorum, and synthesis, and reject or audit-only all other results. Add duplicate-vendor and success-without-attempt-chain regressions.

findings.description: Critical: skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/consensus_synthesizer.py:276 still matches only byte-equal paths with overlapping lines or taxonomy-family plus description tokens; it has no normalized path, symbol, requirement, nearby-location, or synonym evidence and performs unbucketed all-group comparisons. The core differently-worded-reviewer defect remains reproducible and total work is not bounded across vendors.
findings.resolution: Extend Finding and fingerprints with normalized location, affected symbol, and requirement identity; add the owned synonym normalization; bucket candidates by structured evidence before complete-link admission; and add path-normalization, paraphrase, requirement, and maximum-total-work fixtures.

findings.description: Critical: skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_attempts.py:86 locates review-attempt.schema.json only inside this active OpenSpec change, but the portable skill ships no corresponding install asset. A copied installation therefore raises review attempt schema is unavailable and cannot validate any recovery-aware result.
findings.resolution: Ship a stable review-attempt schema under parallel-infrastructure install_assets, resolve that portable asset before proposal-local development paths, and add a copied-install test that executes validate_review_attempt_chain outside this source tree.

findings.description: Critical: skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_attempts.py:314 continues to the next fallback after transient, timeout, configuration, or unknown failure, but its own transition validator permits only invalid-output or capacity retries. Primary capacity followed by fallback-1 transient and fallback-2 valid crashes with only invalid-output or capacity failures may be retried instead of producing a terminal result.
findings.resolution: Stop the fallback loop on every non-recoverable terminal class, preserve the correct terminal outcome, and add multi-fallback tests for transient, timeout, configuration, unknown, and auth failures.

findings.description: Critical: skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py:1829 gives async submit and polling no remaining logical deadline, while review_attempts.py only abandons a daemon thread at timeout. The dispatcher returns a terminal timeout but the poll or SDK call remains alive and can continue consuming subprocess resources and provider spend after the declared bound.
findings.resolution: Propagate the remaining monotonic budget into async submit, every poll subprocess, sleeps, and SDK retry settings; add cooperative cancellation or terminate owned subprocesses/tasks at the outer deadline; verify no review-attempt worker remains alive after timeout.

findings.description: Critical: skills/autopilot/scripts/convergence_loop.py:526 calls dispatch_and_wait without on_terminal_result and does not checkpoint until the whole sequential dispatch returns. A crash after a completed vendor leaves no convergence checkpoint, so the CLI-only progressive persistence fix does not protect the actual autopilot path.
findings.resolution: Install a convergence terminal callback before dispatch that atomically updates the round manifest and vendor index after every logical slot, while retaining the final checkpoint reconciliation. Add a simulated later-vendor crash test.

findings.description: Critical: skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/checkpoint_findings.py:388 accepts caller-supplied quorum_requested and quorum_received without relational validation, permits duplicate vendor index entries, and retains success-only quorum fallbacks for results without attempt evidence. It persisted requested=1 and received=99 unchanged, so malformed checkpoint data can recreate false quorum.
findings.resolution: Validate every attempt chain before persistence, derive requested and received from the logical-slot allocation and distinct eligible terminal vendors, reject duplicate vendors and caller-supplied contradictions, and remove all success-only fallbacks.

findings.description: Critical: skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py:2420 writes progressive manifests with quorum_requested equal to the number of completed slots rather than the scheduled logical-slot count and supplies no partial-round marker. Round 3 visibly persisted requested=1 then 2 while five vendors were scheduled, making crash-recovery evidence indistinguishable from a completed smaller round.
findings.resolution: Persist the stable scheduled logical-slot count from the start of the round, adjust it only for explicit recorded transfers/cancellations, and record partial versus final manifest state so replay cannot treat an interrupted checkpoint as a completed round.

findings.description: Critical: skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py:895 logs raw SDK transient exception text before the attempt sanitizer runs. A transient exception containing token=SUPERSECRET is emitted verbatim, violating the contract that logs and artifacts receive only bounded redacted diagnostics.
findings.resolution: Sanitize and truncate exception details before every logger call and before ReviewResult construction, never log raw SDK exception strings, and add log-capture regressions for token, bearer, API-key, and oversized diagnostics.

findings.description: Critical: skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_routing.py:33 tries only the HTTP bridge and then static routing, hardcodes tier to null, and never attempts the required local archetype source. With HTTP unavailable despite local configuration, Pi falls back to static/null routing; additionally the primary SDK no-key branch in dispatch_and_wait emits a legacy result without a terminal auth attempt chain or replacement eligibility.
findings.resolution: Implement the documented coordinator/public-local-static precedence, preserve archetype/tier/phase provenance from resolution, and route SDK no-key failures through run_vendor_recovery so they produce a validated terminal configuration/auth chain eligible for bounded replacement policy.
